answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity pay an unrecoverable stake before it earns weight. Votes and payouts scale with bonded value plus attested history, so a thousand fresh clones are just a thousand empty ledgers. A swarm must fund every shell and keep it alive across epochs, and that recurring cost grows faster than its size. Picture a wharf where only ships that truly docked get cargo credit, a relic that cannot be forged because the ledger is the relic, and a juniper hedge: single cuttings are cheap, a whole field is not.
